title: sharkd: Align the API with JSON-RPC 2.0
description:
These changes:

* Align the request formats with JSON-RPC
* Align the response formats with JSON-RPC
* Add responses for the requests that currently don’t generate a response
* Continue operation after all request errors

Closes #17235

Oof, this is a big change which makes it harder to review. It will take some time. Can you gradully transform the existing implementation into the final result? It would be nice to have separate commits which:

- Add missing responses, both in the implementation and test (e.g. `test_sharkd_req_follow_bad` in test_sharkd.py).
- Transform the response format to JSON-RPC (impl + tests).

Each commit should be pass tests independently, see https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsdg_html_chunked/ChTestsRunPytest.html how to run and select tests.
If your refactoring manages to pass the existing tests, that would increase confidence in the correctness of the transformation.

Some quick comments based on a quick scan:

- The JSON-RPC spec version is always 2.0, maybe it could be inlined since you have hard-coded `"2.0"` in some places?
- I'll have to check for compliance against the notifications format (i.e. response code 0).
- Some error checking (ws_strtou64) has been removed because it was assumed to be checked before. If so, can that somehow be serialized into a structure or passed as parameter?
- There was a whole `fflush` comment that was stripped. Could the commands for starting/ending a response/error be unified more, possibly while keeping the comment if relevant? (I did not check whether it makes sense to keep the comment.)

@AndersBroman please do not merge until the tests are sorted out.

I am also wondering if this change affects performance somehow (e.g. with many packets).
created #17266 to continue this discussion

Hi @Lekensteyn, My responses in line:

* Add missing responses, both in the implementation and test (e.g. `test_sharkd_req_follow_bad` in test_sharkd.py).
  - Reluctantly, OK.
  - Can you confirm that you want me to make the changes so that sharkd responds with err=0 even when there are problems as this is the way it behaves now?
* Transform the response format to JSON-RPC (impl + tests).
  - OK

* The JSON-RPC spec version is always 2.0, maybe it could be inlined since you have hard-coded `"2.0"` in some places?
  - OK, but what does _inlined_ mean in this context?  Do you mean using a #define?
* I'll have to check for compliance against the notifications format (i.e. response code 0).
  - The spec has a note against the **error** member, "This member MUST NOT exist if there was no error triggered during invocation."
* Some error checking (ws_strtou64) has been removed because it was assumed to be checked before. If so, can that somehow be serialized into a structure or passed as parameter?
  - The idea did cross my mind but that would involve an even bigger change, and I was concerned this may be a step too far for this particular change.  Therefore, I recommend that we do that in a further change rather than include in this one.
* There was a whole `fflush` comment that was stripped. Could the commands for starting/ending a response/error be unified more, possibly while keeping the comment if relevant? (I did not check whether it makes sense to keep the comment.)
  - Yes, I could do that.

* I am also wondering if this change affects performance somehow (e.g. with many packets).
  - Although it increases the size of the response message, there are no changes to the packet processing and so no impact on performance.

PERFORMANCE TEST

| 2 | 22.698s | 23.243s |
| 3 | 22.961s | 23.575s |
| 4 | 22.647s | 23.234s |
| 5 | 22.829s | 23.437s |

INLINE

I have removed the #define SHARKD_JSONRPC_VERSION and inlined the string.

READY TO MERGE

I believe I have now completed the list of pre-requisites above.  The code passes all tests and so is now ready to merge.

commits_data.title: sharkd: Add configuration profile and other options
commits_data.message:
sharkd: Add configuration profile and other options

This change adds code to allow the selection of a configuration
profile during sharkd start by adding a -C command line option.
A new -a option has been added to specify the api service
endpoint e.g. tcp:127.0.0.1:4446

The change also adds version display (-v) and help display (-h) options.

These additions have been made in a way to ensure that the original
command line options still work correctly to maintain backward
compatibility.

The new options have been added using the getopt_long(...) function
that is used by tshark to simplify the addition of further command
line options.

Closes #17222
